infographics.title: The Real 4-File System (After 6 Months of Iteration)
infographics.subtitle: What the diagram doesn't show is what makes it actually work

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md
nodes.description: 6,000 words. Not a brand sheet. An operating manual with error patterns, boundary rules, and session protocol.

nodes.label: MISTAKES.md
nodes.description: 47 entries. 6 HIGH flags. Read FIRST every session. Patterns, not incidents. The file the diagram doesn't show.

nodes.label: AGENT_MAP.md
nodes.description: Two agents, one server, one training pipeline. Each has a boundary: what it can touch, what needs approval.

nodes.label: memory/ (20 files)
nodes.description: User preferences, project state, feedback, references. One file per domain. Single files get stale.

nodes.label: Oracle Rule
nodes.description: Every critical output needs one check the system didn't produce. A test. A second agent. A chain audit.

nodes.label: Kill Protocol
nodes.description: Every session runs one stress scenario. Every failure logs: what broke, why, fix, new MISTAKES entry.

infographics.caption: The diagram shows the happy path. The immune system is what keeps it compounding toward the right answer.

infographics.title: What Actually Compounds

columns.label: What Actually Happens
items: Context cost drops to zero — AI operates from files
Accumulated judgment lives in files, not model weights
Memory splits by domain so only the right file updates
Immune system catches patterns before they compound wrong
Six files minimum — MISTAKES.md is the most important

infographics.caption: The compounding is not intelligence. It is amortized context. By month six, you re-explain nothing.
